History Breitling Premier Chronograph 1950s The company was founded in 1884 by Léon Breitling (1860-1914) in Saint-Imier in the Bernese Jura. In 1892, it was relocated to La Chaux-de-Fonds. In 1914, Gaston Breitling succeeded his father as head of the company. In 1915, the Revue Internationale d'Horlogerie reported a Breitling "chronograph bracelet" with a central chronograph hand and a counter for 30 minutes;[3] chronograph development later became a Breitling focus. This was followed in 1923 by the introduction of the first independent chronograph pusher, and in 1934 by the second independent chronograph pusher, which allowed resetting to zero. From 1936, Breitling supplied the Royal Air Force with on-board watches for its aircraft. They had an eight-day power reserve; the wristwatches developed for pilots featured black dials with eye-catching luminous numerals.[4] In 1942, Breitling launched the Chronomat model, a slide-rule chronograph with manual winding, which was officially introduced by the American forces in the us Army Air Forces. Breitling Navitimer Another development by Breitling's designers was the Navitimer in 1952. A further development of the Chronomat, this pilot's chronograph has an even more complex bezel that allows for more complicated calculations such as fuel consumption, climb or descent rates, average speeds and the like. The company's first diving watch was launched in 1958 under the name Superocean. Shortly before his death in 1979, Willy Breitling sold the rights to the name and brand to pilot and entrepreneur Ernest Schneider. Schneider was no newcomer to the watch market and had already produced watches under the Sicura brand name in the 1960s. After moving manufacturing to Grenchen, Breitling Montres s.a. opened production there in 1982. In 1984, Breitling launched the new Chronomat - the Italian aerobatic team Frecce Tricolori had a significant influence on its development in 1984 - which is now Breitling's main product. Partially based on the Aerospace created in 1985, Breitling launched the Emergency pilot's watch in 1995. In addition to a multifunctional chronograph, this watch integrates an emergency transmitter that sends a widely locatable distress signal on demand on the 121.5 MHz frequency valid for international air traffic. Depending on the national legal situation, this watch could also only be sold to customers with a valid pilot's license. From that point on, Breitling managed the balancing act between producing high-quality mechanical watches and implementing functions that resulted from quartz technology. Since 1999, all Breitling mechanical movements have passed the cosc chronometer test. In 2001, Breitling decided to subject all its electronic movements to cosc testing as well. This means that, as a matter of principle, only chronometers from the factories in La Chaux-de-Fonds and Grenchen are now sold. In 2002, the production of mechanical watches was outsourced to La Chaux-de-Fonds, the place where the company was already located in 1892. Also in 2002, Breitling became the first manufacturer to produce a mechanical diver's watch water-resistant to 3000 meters. For its 125th anniversary in 2009, Breitling presented a self-constructed and self-manufactured ("in-house") chronograph movement under the designation "B01" at Baselworld. This movement was also cosc-certified. At the end of April 2017, the British financial investor cvc Capital Partners acquired 80 percent of the shares in Breitling; the owner family around Theodore Schneider retained 20 percent. In July 2017, the former watchmaking boss of Richemont, Georges Kern, became the new head of Breitling. In November 2018, the remaining 20 percent of the shares were also sold to cvc. Georges Kern also holds a stake in the company. Sponsoring Aeronautics Breitling Super Constellation at Mollis airfield in Switzerland (2011). Breitling has quite a few historical connections with aviation, such as equipping the British Air Force with on-board watches, or the recoendation of the Navitimer as a pilot's watch by the aopa in 1952. Another example was astronaut Scott Carpenter, who flew around the Earth aboard the Aurora 7 capsule in May 1962 wearing a Breitling Cosmonaute. The distinctive feature of this watch is a 24-hour display on the central dial. This feature would have allowed the wearer to distinguish between, say, 01:00 and 13:00 of the respective reference time during longer missions. For Carpenter, this display was presumably of no use at all, since he was already in the North Atlantic on schedule after three orbits of 45 minutes each and a total flight duration of just under five hours. During the Apollo program, nasa did not attach any importance to this wristwatch function, despite mission durations of over a week. Breitling, like Fortis and Tutima among others, maintained close contacts with military aviation squadrons as well as with well-known aerobatic squadrons. After many decades of pilots' dependence on precise mechanical watches, this liaison served mainly to enhance their image. Today, high-quality mechanical aviation chronographs have more of a decorative character and serve pilots to illustrate their traditions as well as their professional self-image. In fact, around 2001, only about 5% of all watches manufactured by Breitling were bought by pilots. Breitling also sponsored the first successful circumnavigation of the earth in a balloon, the Breitling Orbiter 3, by Brian Jones and Bertrand Piccard. They succeeded in circumnavigating the globe from March 1, 1999 (take-off in Switzerland) to March 21, 1999 (landing in Egypt) without stopping in less than 20 days. In addition, Breitling sponsored the world's last Super Constellation still certified for passenger flights even before its matriculation in Switzerland in 2007 until 2017, which is why this aircraft flew almost continuously with the Breitling Super Constellation inscription. Triathlon With the "Breitling Triathlon Squad," Breitling created a team of athletes at the beginning of 2018, consisting of three people who are among the best in the world in their fields - Switzerland's Daniela Ryf, Germany's Jan Frodeno, and Australia's Chris McCormack. Breitling's advertising campaign also featured a "Cinema Squad" with Brad Pitt, Charlize Theron and Adam Driver. In the 1970s and 1980s, Serge Gainsbourg had been a brand ambassador.
